title: Super-Human Performance in Gran Turismo Sport Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a learning-based system for autonomous car racing in Gran Turismo Sport, achieving super-human performance by leveraging deep reinforcement learning and a course-progress proxy reward.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're playing a racing game, and you want to finish the track as fast as possible. Classical approaches would plan the optimal trajectory and then control the car to follow it. However, this can be complex and limited. Our approach uses deep reinforcement learning to directly map observations to control commands, allowing for more flexible and adaptive control.

We use a proxy reward based on the course progress, which helps the agent learn to drive faster and more efficiently.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
Our system uses a neural network policy to map input states to actions. We optimize the policy parameters using the soft actor-critic algorithm and a replay buffer. The policy network takes in features such as the car's velocity, acceleration, and distance to the track's edge, and outputs the steering angle and throttle-brake signal.

We also introduce a second reward term to penalize wall contact, which helps the agent learn to avoid collisions.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluate our approach in three race settings, featuring different cars and tracks. Our approach outperforms the best human lap time in all three settings, with a margin of 0.15 and 0.04 seconds for settings A and B, respectively.

The results show that our approach can achieve super-human performance in autonomous car racing.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Our approach has implications for the development of autonomous vehicles, as it demonstrates the potential for deep reinforcement learning to achieve super-human performance in complex tasks.

The use of a course-progress proxy reward and a neural network policy allows for more flexible and adaptive control, which can be applied to a wide range of autonomous driving scenarios.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our approach introduces several key innovations, including the use of a course-progress proxy reward and a neural network policy.

The use of a replay buffer and the soft actor-critic algorithm allows for efficient optimization of the policy parameters, and the introduction of a second reward term to penalize wall contact helps the agent learn to avoid collisions.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try our approach, you can use a similar setup and train your own policy using the soft actor-critic algorithm and a replay buffer.

You can also experiment with different reward functions and neural network architectures to see how they affect the performance of the agent.
